minutes.headline: Committee set a quarter-two final deadline for learning-model changes and backed applying for E-rate bandwidth upgrades.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the NEASC accreditation report, the superintendent's draft goals, and an IT plan to upgrade internet at the primary school and Turkey Hill. It voted to let families change learning models once more for quarter two, then stay put, and heard the business manager say no extra town money is needed for FY21 covid costs. Fall athletics and committee reports followed.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted to let families change learning model once more for quarter two, with a midnight October 19 deadline, then stay put barring case-by-case circumstances.
The committee voted 5-0 by roll call to have the administration apply for E-rate funds and begin looking into internet bandwidth upgrades.
The business manager reported no extra town money is needed for FY21 covid costs, and the committee voted to accept the budget report.
The superintendent will finalize the draft goals and send a rubric for members' individual feedback after the committee reviewed them.
Upgrades to internet connections are monthly service contracts that must come from the operating budget, while new firewall routers were bought with CARES Act funds.

why_it_matters: Families with children in the district have one last window to switch between learning models before quarter two, so a choice made now generally holds.
Faster internet at the primary school and Turkey Hill would become an ongoing operating-budget cost, and the E-rate discount decides how large that cost is.
